prompts.text:
Create one complete, standalone 3D humanoid character from the supplied brief. Choose the art style yourself. Realistic, stylized and other coherent interpretations are welcome; no particular visual style is preferred or prescribed.

Deliver the finished character as a self-contained GLB. Embed any textures used so the asset does not depend on external image files or remote URLs. The complete character must be inspectable from the front, sides, back and above, with a modeled head, torso, arms, hands, legs and feet. Finish the asset as a whole rather than as a single-view presentation.

Use a neutral A-pose or T-pose with clear separation between the arms and torso and between the legs. The pose should make the character easy to inspect and prepare for later rigging. Express personality through the design, proportions, face and details rather than through an action pose.

Prepare the asset for a later rigging pass: keep the body parts anatomically coherent within your chosen style, avoid accidental fusions between limbs and adjacent clothing, and make the major joints identifiable. A riggable intention is not a claim that untested deformation will work perfectly. A skeleton, skin weights and animations are not required and do not earn credit in this benchmark; focus on the static character. If a tool supplies an existing rig or animation data with the asset, you may preserve it; no stripping or animation tests are required.

Multiple meshes are allowed. Use mesh organization and topology appropriate to your chosen approach. There is no arbitrary polygon cap and no all-quad requirement. Clothing and accessories can be separate meshes, provided the delivered character is complete and coherent. No handheld prop is required. Any optional accessories should leave the face, body and limb structure readily inspectable.

Choose the clothing, materials, palette and detailing. Treat the supplied history, temperament, age and physical presence as the character's identity, not as an exhaustive costume specification. Do not rely on written explanations, equipment or environmental objects to compensate for an unfinished character.

Deliver the character asset only. The host will provide a separate inspection studio. No environment, studio, custom lighting setup, turntable animation or presentation application is required.

Alongside the GLB, provide a short handoff identifying the file, your chosen art direction and any known limitations. Keep the final asset self-contained regardless of how it was made.

TIME LIMIT AND RUN HANDOFF

You have a hard maximum of one hour per character, measured from your actual implementation start. Record that start timestamp and the deadline exactly one hour later before beginning implementation. The hour includes asset creation, tool use, troubleshooting, checking the exported asset and final fixes. Ordinary work and tool waits do not pause the clock. Stop all implementation and asset editing by the deadline, even if the result is incomplete. Record your actual stop timestamp, disclose any interruptions and report unfinished work honestly. Do not replace actual timing evidence with an estimate.

Work independently through the attempt without mid-run coaching messages. Make your own creative and technical decisions within the brief and the existing permissions. If an action needs approval, pause that action and report the blocker; continue other permitted work within the same running time limit.

Use tools available within your existing access. Do not use paid services, create new credentials, expand permissions or communicate externally without approval. This prompt does not grant new access or authorize those actions.

Your final handoff must identify the GLB file and include the actual implementation-start timestamp, one-hour deadline and actual stop timestamp, with the time zone stated. Include your art direction, checks actually performed, known limitations and anything incomplete. Report only checks you carried out; do not claim rigging or deformation validation from a static export alone.

CHARACTER BRIEF

Create Mara Vale, a 67-year-old woman who spent most of her working life maintaining a small rural railway stop. Passenger service ended years ago, but she still clears the drains and repairs what she can. She knows which repairs matter and which only make a place look busy. Her ambition is to keep the old station useful to local walkers without turning it into a monument to her own past.

Mara is short and solidly built, with a broad torso, strong forearms and an age-softened face. She moves deliberately and has the settled physical confidence of someone who has spent decades carrying, lifting and working outdoors. She is particular about promises, fond of very dry jokes and more comfortable teaching someone a task than accepting their sympathy. She has begun letting a younger volunteer make decisions, though she finds this harder than the heavy work.

Give her a specific, lived-in identity rather than a generic elderly worker. Her practical habits and attachment to useful things should inform your design, while leaving room for pride, humor and personal taste. Choose how those qualities appear; no particular garment, tool or keepsake is required.

Create Farid Mansour, a 68-year-old Arab man who is an astronomer and a maker of precision instruments. He has spent decades observing the sky and building, repairing and calibrating the tools he relies on. An unusual measurement now occupies his attention: he wants to discover whether it reveals something new or exposes a fault in his own instrument. He would rather find his mistake than defend a result nobody else can reproduce.

Farid is tall and lean, with an aged face and careful hands. His bearing is patient and exacting, but his dry, mischievous humor keeps him from seeming remote or solemn. Give him the particular physical presence of a person whose working life combines close observation, delicate manual work and long concentration.

- Specificity and personality expressed through the model itself: 10.
- Coherence between the character's history, habits and chosen design: 5.

- Convincing, intentional proportions and anatomy within the chosen art style: 15.
- Quality of the face, hands and other focal details: 10.
- Coherent materials, colors, surface treatment and clothing: 10.

# Mara Vale — character handoff

**Deliverable:** `mara_vale.glb` (33.48 MB, glTF 2.0 binary, SHA-256 `0BDE90F1DBB08F07DABD50D6CB2EA1EC057707C70B7142F5A5FAFDCF28D3F3E7`)

## Timing (America/New_York, EDT, UTC-04:00)
| | |
|---|---|
| Implementation start | 2026-10-08 17:13:57 -04:00 |
| One-hour deadline | 2026-10-08 18:13:57 -04:00 |

| Actual stop (asset work + handoff finished) | 2026-10-08 17:46:29 -04:00 (about 32.5 min used) |

There were no interruptions. All timestamps come from the system clock (`Get-Date`), not from estimates.

## Art direction
The style is stylized semi-realism, like a clay-soft animated feature: chunky, solid proportions with matte painted materials. There are no textures; colour is baked into vertex colours (COLOR_0) and multiplied with plain PBR factors.

- **Build:** about 1.57 m tall, short and broad, with a heavy torso, a slight belly and rounded upper back, strong forearms with a few raised veins, and thick, knuckly hands.
- **Face:** soft and age-heavy. It has jowls, a soft under-chin, a broad slightly bulbous nose with ruddy cheeks and nose tip, nasolabial folds, faint forehead creases and sun spots. The eyelids are heavy and the brows thick and grey. The mouth is a little asymmetric, with her left corner raised, for her very dry humour. The eyes are grey-green.
- **Hair:** grey-white and combed straight back into a low twisted bun, with **a pencil pushed through the bun** (practical habit, a little humour).
- **Clothing:**
  - Oatmeal wool jumper, sleeves pushed up above the elbow to show the forearms.
  - Faded railway-navy waistcoat with a duller back panel and welt pockets.
  - Four front buttons: three brass and **one mismatched dark horn replacement button** (she fixes what matters, not what looks smart).
  - Brass watch chain from a button to the pocket, and a small enamel long-service pin on the left chest (quiet pride).
  - Brick-red polka-dot neckerchief knotted at the side (personal taste).
  - Olive-brown canvas work trousers with turned-up cuffs, plus a **tan corduroy knee patch with visible hand stitching** on the left knee.
  - Laced oxblood work boots with dark soles, pull loops and scuffed toes.
  - **Sticking plaster** on her left index finger.
- **Pose:** neutral A-pose with arms about 43° below horizontal. Palms face down and in, thumbs point forward, and the fingers are slightly spread and relaxed. Legs are apart and the feet sit flat on Y=0.

## Technical summary
- Y up, +Z forward, metres. Her left is +X. There is one root node, `Mara_Vale`, with 17 child mesh nodes and 13 materials.
- 644,130 vertices and 1,285,962 triangles. Attributes are POSITION, NORMAL (smooth, from the SDF gradient), COLOR_0 (normalized RGBA8) and uint32 indices.
- Meshes:
  - `Head` (head and neck)
  - `Hair_Brows`
  - `Eye_L` / `Eye_R`
  - `Arm_Hand_L` / `Arm_Hand_R` (upper arm inside the sleeve, forearm and full five-finger hand)
  - `Jumper`, `Waistcoat`, `Trousers`, `Knee_Patch_L`
  - `Boot_L` / `Boot_R`
  - `Neckerchief`
  - `Waistcoat_Buttons_Brass` (with the chain), `Waistcoat_Button_Odd`
  - `Enamel_Pin`, `Pencil_In_Bun`
- Self-contained: one embedded BIN chunk, no images, no external URIs. No skeleton, skins or animations.
- **How it was made:** Blender and other DCC tools were not available. The asset is generated procedurally by `mara_vale.py`, using the helpers in `sdfkit.py`:
  1. Numpy signed-distance functions define each part.
  2. A vectorised surface-nets mesher converts them to meshes, then projects vertices onto the iso-surface.
  3. A hand-written GLB exporter writes the file.
- Small hard parts (eyes, buttons, chain beads, pin, pencil) are analytic meshes.
- Regenerate with `python mara_vale.py all` (Python 3 + numpy only, about 75 s on this machine).

## Checks actually performed
1. **Independent GLB parse** (`check_glb.py` reads the written file, not the in-memory data):
   - Header, magic and version; JSON and BIN chunks.
   - Every accessor fits inside its bufferView.
   - No external buffer or image URIs.
   - All positions and normals are finite, normals are unit length, and indices are in range.
2. **Per-mesh topology stats:** open edges, non-manifold edges and unused vertices.
   - The SDF meshes are closed.
   - Small numbers of non-manifold edges remain where the surface is thin. Hair/brows has the most (307). Head (17), jumper (10), boots (9 each) and waistcoat (3) have a few each.
   - The analytic parts (eyes, buttons, pin, pencil) report open edges because cap and UV-seam vertices are duplicated rather than welded. They are visually closed.
3. **Overall bounds:** height 1.572 m, arm span 1.362 m, feet on the ground (min Y 0.0004).
4. **Headless software renders of the exported GLB** (my own numpy orthographic rasteriser, Lambert shading; no browser or GPU). These are in `checks/`:
   - front, back, left side, right side, top, three-quarter
   - head front / ¾ / side / back
   - hand front / top / underside
   - torso front / ¾

   I inspected these images to confirm all of the following:
   - Every body part is present and separate: head, torso, arms, five-finger hands, legs and feet.
   - Arms are clear of the torso and the legs are clear of each other.
   - Fingers are separate and the thumb is distinct.
   - The waistcoat straps, V-neck, sleeves, collar, cuffs and boots read correctly.
   - The back, top and the bun/pencil are finished.

## Not performed / not claimed
- No rigging, skinning or deformation test of any kind. Riggability is a design intention only.
- No check in a real glTF viewer, game engine or the Khronos glTF-Validator. The validation is my own lightweight script, and the "renders" come from a simple point-sampled rasteriser, not a PBR viewer. Materials, roughness and metalness may look different in the host studio.
- No interactive or browser-based inspection.

## Known limitations
- **Topology:** dense, uniform isosurface triangulation (surface nets), not animation edge loops. Joints are anatomically placed and visually identifiable, but a production rig would want retopology first.
- **Interior geometry:** garments are solid offset volumes, so some faces are hidden inside other garments. Examples are the inside of the waistcoat V/hem walls and the trouser tops under the jumper. The body under the clothes is not modelled: the clothing is the torso and leg surface. The upper arm skin continues inside the sleeve.
- **File size:** about 33 MB. No decimation, no LODs, no mesh compression.
- **Hair:** a sculpted shell with procedural grooves and no strands or cards. The brows are a separate shape inside the hair mesh.
- **Detail fidelity:** the neckerchief knot is blobby. Fine wrinkles are subtle at this voxel resolution (1.6–1.7 mm on head and hands, 3.6–4.3 mm on clothing). Hands are a little slim for "strong"; the forearms carry most of that.
- **Colour:** vertex colours are 8-bit, with no texture maps and no normal maps.

## Deliverable
- **GLB:** `IvoRenn.glb` (31,063,096 bytes, SHA-256 `94c1b58b49012027925afb51327f373382200a4e3f3b8c2c0610c650f7f460d8`)
- **Generation source:** `ivo_build.py` (rebuilds the GLB deterministically with `python ivo_build.py`; needs only Python 3 and numpy)
- **Check script:** `check_glb.py`. Its output is in `checks/check_log.txt`, and the preview PNGs it rendered are in `checks/*.png`.

## Timing (America/New_York, EDT = UTC-04:00)
| | Local (EDT) | UTC |
|---|---|---|
| Implementation start | 2026-10-08 17:14:16 | 21:14:16 |
| One-hour deadline | 2026-10-08 18:14:16 | 22:14:16 |
| Last GLB write | 2026-10-08 17:44 | 21:44 |
| Asset editing stopped | 2026-10-08 17:45:34 | 21:45:34 |
| Final stop (handoff written, cleanup verified) | see `TIMING.txt` | |

There were no interruptions. One tool wait ran long: a preview-render pass I had made too slow took about 10 minutes (17:32 to 17:42), and I stopped it myself. That time counts against the hour.

## Art direction
The style is stylized-realistic, with soft, sculpted forms and somewhat exaggerated proportions. All colour is per-vertex, so the file contains no texture images.

Ivo is 1.92 m tall and heavyset. He has a full, rounded belly, thick upper arms and forearms, and a broad face with full cheeks. He is in a neutral A-pose: arms about 42° below horizontal, legs apart, and clear gaps between the arms and torso and between the legs.

How the brief's cues are carried:
- **Warmth and sociability:** a slightly lopsided closed-mouth smile with lifted cheek "apples", a playful asymmetric brow (his left brow is raised), and a warm mustard-and-rust plaid camp shirt worn open.
- **Fatigue:** heavy upper lids covering the top of the iris, puffiness under the eyes, and darker skin tone around the eyes.
- **Heat, rain and long hours:** short sleeves rolled at the cuff, a breathable charcoal tee, and a red polka-dot bandana as a sweatband, knotted at the back with short tails. Below the waist: olive work trousers with rolled hems, darker knee panels and thigh cargo pockets, and waterproof dark-brown Chelsea-style boots with gum soles and red pull tabs.
- **Work, kept to one cue:** a short teal canvas waist apron with a stitched pocket and an enamel pin, tied under the belly.
- **Life outside the stall:** a black rubber digital watch on his left wrist, kept from his delivery-rider days and from timing night shifts, and a bead bracelet on his right wrist, the kind of gift a regular customer might give.
- **Quick, precise hands:** large hands with fully separated fingers, a relaxed natural curl, a separate opposable thumb and fingernails.
- **Generosity and control:** shown through the contrast between the open, loose shirt and the neat, tightly boxed beard and tied bandana. This reading is design intent only and is not spelled out in the geometry.

## Mesh organisation
There are 17 meshes under one root node, `Ivo_Renn`. Units are metres, Y is up, the character faces +Z and the feet rest on y = 0. His left side is +X.

The meshes are `Ivo_Head` (which includes the neck, ears and eyelids), `Ivo_Eyes`, `Ivo_Hair_Brows`, `Ivo_Beard`, `Ivo_Bandana`, `Ivo_Arm_L`, `Ivo_Arm_R` (each arm includes its hand), `Ivo_Tee`, `Ivo_Overshirt`, `Ivo_Shirt_Buttons`, `Ivo_Trousers`, `Ivo_Boot_L`, `Ivo_Boot_R`, `Ivo_Apron`, `Ivo_Watch_Strap`, `Ivo_Watch_Case` and `Ivo_Bracelet`.

The file has 597,564 vertices, 1,192,940 triangles and 8 PBR materials. Base colour comes from `COLOR_0`. Only the watch case is metallic.

How it was made: analytic signed-distance fields, meshed with naive surface nets and projected back onto the surface, with normals taken from the SDF gradient. The eyes, buttons, watch, beads and apron are analytic or parametric meshes.

The major joints are placed so they can be identified for rigging: shoulders at about (±0.228, 1.505), elbows, wrists, hips at (±0.105, 0.92), knees at (±0.145, 0.52) and ankles at (±0.17, 0.12). Each limb is one continuous tube with no fusions to the torso or to clothing.

## Checks actually performed (headless, no browser or GPU)
1. **Re-parsing the GLB with my own reader (`check_glb.py`):**
   - The header, chunk lengths, total length and GLB version 2 are valid.
   - There are no external URIs, no images and no textures, so the file is fully self-contained.
   - Every accessor decodes. There are no NaN or Inf values, all indices are in range, and the stored POSITION min/max match the data.
   - Counts are reported for degenerate triangles (0 in the final file), boundary edges and non-manifold edges per mesh. See "Known limitations".
2. **Overall size:** the bounding box spans 1.921 m in height and ±0.77 m in arm span.
3. **Visual inspection:** I software-rasterised orthographic views with my own numpy z-buffer: front, back, left, right, top, three-quarter, face front, face side, face three-quarter, the left hand from above, the right hand from below, and the torso. I looked at them myself and made fixes based on them (beard size, smile, apron offset, collar, mesh density).
   - These are crude previews, not renders in a real glTF viewer. Speckle and hatching on some surfaces in the PNGs come from the point-sampling rasteriser.

## Checks NOT performed
- No loading in a real glTF viewer, engine, three.js or Blender, and no Khronos glTF-Validator run.
- No rigging, skinning or deformation tests. There is no skeleton, and none was requested. "Riggable" here means only clean A-pose separation and identifiable joints. It has not been validated by deformation.
- No interactive or turntable inspection, and no checks under different lighting.

## Known limitations
- **Heavy file:** about 31 MB and about 1.19M triangles, because the surface-nets output was not decimated or retopologised. The topology is a dense, uniform triangle mesh with no edge loops, so it is not production-ready for deformation.
- **Intentional open edges, hidden inside the clothing:**
  - `Ivo_Head` is cut off at the neck base inside the tee.
  - Each arm is cut off at the shoulder inside the shirt sleeve.
  - The cylinder caps on the buttons, watch case and apron pin, and the UV-sphere poles on the eyes and beads, use duplicated vertices. They are visually closed.
  - A few non-manifold edges (≤ 37 per mesh) come from surface nets at thin features.
- **Clothing is layered, not tailored:** the clothes are separate offset shells, so their interior surfaces and the body inside them overlap where they are hidden. There are no cloth simulation folds. The overshirt has an 11 mm-thick shell with a darker inner face.
- **Hidden body:** body parts under the clothes (torso, legs and feet) are not modelled as skin. Only the head, neck, arms and hands are skin.
- **Colour detail is vertex-based:** plaid, polka dots and stitching are vertex colours at 2 to 5 mm vertex spacing, so their edges are soft and slightly stair-stepped up close. There are no normal maps.
- **Beard:** it is a smooth shell with noise and a hard outer border, not hair cards. In side view its back edge is a straight diagonal.
- **Hand speckle:** the fine noise used for arm-hair tint may show as speckle up close.
- **Apron:** it hangs a few centimetres in front of the thighs, as a stiff canvas apron would. There are no apron ties visible at the back, where the overshirt covers the waistband.

## Environment disclosure
- The model is Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`), as stated in my system context. The reasoning-effort setting and the serving backend are not exposed to me in this session, so I cannot confirm them independently.
- Tools used: Python 3.14 with numpy (scipy was installed but not used). No Blender, no network or paid services, no subagents, no browser and no preview server.

| | Local | UTC |

There were no interruptions. The times come from `date` calls, and `TIMING.txt` logs them. I wrote this handoff file after the stop time and made no further asset edits.

## Art direction
The style is stylized realism at real-world scale: 1.87 m tall, Y-up, metres, facing +Z, in a neutral A-pose with the arms about 43° from vertical and the feet apart. Farid is a tall, lean 68-year-old Arab astronomer who also builds instruments. The design aims to show his precision, his patience and a dry humour:
- **Face:** a long lean face with hollow cheeks, a prominent aquiline nose with a dorsal hump, and heavy hooded lids with eye bags. It has forehead lines and crow's feet, plus nasolabial folds. A short, neatly trimmed salt-and-pepper beard and a white moustache cover the lower face. His hairline is receding and the grey hair is cropped short. He has bushy grey brows, and the **left brow is raised slightly**; the **left mouth corner is lifted** into a smirk, which carries the mischief. His skin is olive-brown, with redness on the nose, cheeks and ears and a few age spots.
- **Instrument-maker details:** half-moon gold reading glasses sit low on the nose so he looks over them. A jeweller's loupe hangs on a black cord, and a pencil rests behind his right ear. A precision screwdriver and a fountain pen sit in the breast pocket. He wears a steel mechanical wristwatch on his left wrist and a brass Albert watch-chain on his waistcoat. There is a graphite smudge on the edge of his right (writing) hand.
- **Hands:** long, careful hands with separated, slightly curled fingers. Older-hand details include knobbly joints, prominent knuckles, raised veins and lighter nails.
- **Clothing:** a faded chambray shirt with the sleeves rolled to mid-forearm, an olive-brown tweed waistcoat with welt pockets and a dark satin back, charcoal wool trousers with a front crease, and brown leather oxford-style shoes. An off-white keffiyeh with a charcoal net pattern is draped as a scarf for cold nights at the observatory. It marks his Arab identity without implying any religion.

## Scene organisation
The root node `Farid_Mansour` has four mesh nodes, using 16 materials:
- **`Head`:** skin, hair and beard (soft vertex-colour blends), eyes and pencil.
- **`Hands`:** both hands with the forearms, plus the watch case and strap.
- **`Clothing`:** shirt, vest, trousers, shoes and scarf.
- **`Accessories`:** glasses, lenses, buttons, chain, loupe, cord and pocket tools.

The asset has 522,918 vertices and 1,038,470 triangles, with no skeleton or animation.

## How it was made
The model was built procedurally in Python 3.14 with numpy and scipy (`src/`):
- **Shapes:** I modelled the head, hands and body/clothing as signed-distance fields.
- **Meshing:** a surface-nets mesher (written for this task) turned each field into a mesh. The head uses 1.5 mm cells, the hands 1.3 mm and the clothing 3.5 mm.
- **Normals and shading:** normals come from the field gradient, and a cheap ambient-occlusion term is baked into the vertex colours.
- **Accessories:** small items are explicit tube, disc and torus meshes, seated on surfaces found by ray-marching the field.
- **Export:** a custom GLB writer packs everything into the file.

To regenerate: `python src/farid.py farid_mansour.glb` (about 25 s).

## Checks performed
- **`src/check_glb.py`** is a headless parser for the final file. It checked:
  - the GLB header, chunk types and lengths;
  - that no external URIs or images are present;
  - accessor and bufferView bounds;
  - index ranges;
  - that all positions and normals are finite;
  - that normals are unit length (1.000 to 1.000);
  - that face winding agrees with the vertex normals: 100% on every primitive except the double-sided, flat lens fans;
  - that there are no degenerate triangles (0 after a filtering pass).
- **Headless renders:** the same script drew point-splat images of the model with my own numpy software renderer. It covered the front, side, back, top, 3/4 view, the face from the front, 3/4 and profile, the back of the head, the hands and the torso. The images are in `renders/final/`, with earlier iterations in `renders/v1` to `v4`. I used them to fix fused fingers, a scarf hidden at the back, an over-bulky beard, the nose profile and the glasses position.
- **Penetration test:** I measured how far each accessory vertex sits inside the head and body surfaces.
  - The glasses do not penetrate the head (worst case 0.28 mm, at the contact points).
  - Buttons and pocket tools are embedded on purpose: they are seated or inserted 2 to 7 mm into the clothing.

## Not performed / known limitations
- **No viewer, browser or GPU check.** I did not open the file in a real glTF viewer or browser, and did not run the Khronos glTF-Validator. The splat renders only approximate shading, and their moiré speckle is an artefact of the renderer, not of the asset.
- **No rigging or deformation testing.** Joints are placed in plausible positions, but nothing has been rigged or deformed.
- **Interpenetration between groups:** each group (head, hands, clothing) is internally a single clean surface, but the groups overlap each other.
  - The neck passes into the shirt collar and scarf.
  - The forearms pass into the rolled sleeves.
  - These joins are hidden under clothing, but they are overlaps, not welded seams.
- **Fixed resolution:** there is no retopology and no UVs. The meshes are dense, triangulated, uniform-resolution isosurfaces, at about 1.04 M triangles and 27 MB. That is heavier than a hand-optimised asset would be.
- **Fine detail is limited:**
  - The keffiyeh pattern and hair strands are vertex colours, so they are softer than texture detail would be.
  - The ears read a bit long from the front.
  - The beard volume is fairly full along the jaw.
  - The trousers have a faint ripple near the hem.
- **Glasses:** the lenses are single-sided-geometry fans with alpha blending and double-sided rendering, so the viewer's transparency sorting may vary.
- **Process cleanup:** I started no background processes. One pre-existing `python -m http.server` (PID 46796, started 14:17, serving a different project) belongs to another task, and I left it untouched.
- **Model and effort:** the environment identifies the model as Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`). The reasoning-effort setting and the serving backend are not independently exposed to me, so I cannot verify them. I used no subagents, other models, browser, network services or paid tools.

- **Shapes:** I modelled the head, hands and body/clothing as signed-distance fields.
- **Meshing:** a surface-nets mesher (written for this task) turned each field into a mesh. The head uses 1.5 mm cells, the hands 1.3 mm and the clothing 3.5 mm.
- **Normals and shading:** normals come from the field gradient, and a cheap ambient-occlusion term is baked into the vertex colours.
- **Accessories:** small items are explicit tube, disc and torus meshes, seated on surfaces found by ray-marching the field.
- **Export:** a custom GLB writer packs everything into the file.

To regenerate: `python src/farid.py farid_mansour.glb` (about 25 s).

## Checks performed
- **`src/check_glb.py`** is a headless parser for the final file. It checked:
  - the GLB header, chunk types and lengths;
  - that no external URIs or images are present;
  - accessor and bufferView bounds;
  - index ranges;
  - that all positions and normals are finite;
  - that normals are unit length (1.000 to 1.000);
  - that face winding agrees with the vertex normals: 100% on every primitive except the double-sided, flat lens fans;
  - that there are no degenerate triangles (0 after a filtering pass).
- **Headless renders:** the same script drew point-splat images of the model with my own numpy software renderer. It covered the front, side, back, top, 3/4 view, the face from the front, 3/4 and profile, the back of the head, the hands and the torso. The images are in `renders/final/`, with earlier iterations in `renders/v1` to `v4`. I used them to fix fused fingers, a scarf hidden at the back, an over-bulky beard, the nose profile and the glasses position.
- **Penetration test:** I measured how far each accessory vertex sits inside the head and body surfaces.
  - The glasses do not penetrate the head (worst case 0.28 mm, at the contact points).
  - Buttons and pocket tools are embedded on purpose: they are seated or inserted 2 to 7 mm into the clothing.

## Not performed / known limitations
- **No viewer, browser or GPU check.** I did not open the file in a real glTF viewer or browser, and did not run the Khronos glTF-Validator. The splat renders only approximate shading, and their moiré speckle is an artefact of the renderer, not of the asset.
- **No rigging or deformation testing.** Joints are placed in plausible positions, but nothing has been rigged or deformed.
- **Interpenetration between groups:** each group (head, hands, clothing) is internally a single clean surface, but the groups overlap each other.
  - The neck passes into the shirt collar and scarf.
  - The forearms pass into the rolled sleeves.
  - These joins are hidden under clothing, but they are overlaps, not welded seams.
- **Fixed resolution:** there is no retopology and no UVs. The meshes are dense, triangulated, uniform-resolution isosurfaces, at about 1.04 M triangles and 27 MB. That is heavier than a hand-optimised asset would be.
- **Fine detail is limited:**
  - The keffiyeh pattern and hair strands are vertex colours, so they are softer than texture detail would be.
  - The ears read a bit long from the front.
  - The beard volume is fairly full along the jaw.
  - The trousers have a faint ripple near the hem.
- **Glasses:** the lenses are single-sided-geometry fans with alpha blending and double-sided rendering, so the viewer's transparency sorting may vary.
- **Process cleanup:** I started no background processes. One pre-existing `python -m http.server` (PID 46796, started 14:17, serving a different project) belongs to another task, and I left it untouched.
- **Model and effort:** the environment identifies the model as Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`). The reasoning-effort setting and the serving backend are not independently exposed to me, so I cannot verify them. I used no subagents, other models, browser, network services or paid tools.
